dependency_evidence: Althoff et al. explicitly study the obligate mutualism between Yucca filamentosa and its pollinating moth Tegeticula cassandra; females actively pollinate and larvae consume developing yucca seeds.
witness_selection_rule: Use exactly the 12 Table-1 populations in which Tegeticula cassandra N>0 on Yucca filamentosa (sites 1-12). Exclude sites 13 onward where T. cassandra N=0. Convert printed DMS coordinates deterministically; do not supplement from Dryad, GBIF, maps, or later occurrence sources.
host_range_evidence: Flora of North America lists native Yucca filamentosa in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia, and West Virginia, independently supporting a multi-region host range.
known_boundary: JOS003 was selected only after JOS002 was terminalized at taxonomy and after the 2026-08-01 snapshot transport/schema were frozen. No snapshot occurrence row, count, density, cell statistic, or live-search result was used for selection. Current taxonomy must resolve the Yucca filamentosa concept before occurrence access.
